title: Only 7% Pass This Midwifery Entrance Exam
summary: Connect pregnancy, birth, newborn care and clear communication through practical clues.

landing.intro:
Read the clues. Make the connections.
Put your thinking to the test.

about.body:
Explore pregnancy physiology, birth, newborn wellbeing, observation and respectful care. Each set introduces a new topic and a fresh checkpoint.

Choose the answer best supported by the information given. Your overall result includes topic strengths and an optional review of missed answers.

The questions use broad principles that do not depend on one country’s maternity pathway. Any real concern needs qualified maternity advice; this entertainment quiz is not a clinical assessment or an accredited entrance examination.

steps: Read the clues and choose one answer.
See your topic profile at each checkpoint and continue to a new challenge.
Reveal your overall result, then optionally review the answers you missed.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an accredited midwifery entrance examination, clinical assessment, professional qualification or medical advice. Maternity-care procedures and responsibilities vary; always follow local policy and qualified clinical guidance.

midwifery-s1q1.question: Which organ supports exchange between the pregnant person and the developing baby?

midwifery-s1q2.question: Where does a baby normally develop during pregnancy?

midwifery-s1q3.question: What connects the baby to the placenta?

midwifery-s1q4.question: What is one main role of amniotic fluid?

midwifery-s1q5.question: Which structure is the lower opening of the uterus?

midwifery-s1q6.question: Before birth, oxygen normally reaches the baby through which route?

answers.a2: Placental exchange and the umbilical cord
answers.a3: Air breathed directly through the mouth

midwifery-s1q7.question: Which organ provides the muscular contractions of childbirth?

midwifery-s2q1.question: What does antenatal or prenatal care mean?

midwifery-s2q2.question: A severe new headache occurs with visual changes during pregnancy. What is safest?

answers.a3: Wait for the next routine appointment

midwifery-s2q3.question: A baby’s usual movement pattern slows noticeably. What is the safest response?

answers.a1: Assume all babies stop moving before birth
answers.a2: Wait several days to see a pattern
answers.a3: Contact a qualified maternity service promptly
answers.a4: Rely only on another person’s experience

midwifery-s2q4.question: Why ask about current medicines at a pregnancy appointment?

answers.a1: To support an informed review of their suitability
answers.a2: To replace the rest of the assessment
answers.a4: To select treatment from the package colour

midwifery-s2q5.question: Which report needs urgent attention during pregnancy?

answers.a1: A change in the appointment room
answers.a2: A request to reschedule a routine class
answers.a3: A question about the clinic’s opening time
answers.a4: Sudden severe chest pain or trouble breathing

midwifery-s2q6.question: A pregnant person reports persistent vomiting and cannot keep fluids down. What is safest?

answers.a3: Treat a normal earlier visit as proof all is well

midwifery-s2q7.question: Why should a new concern still be assessed after an earlier normal appointment?

answers.a2: Every new symptom proves the same diagnosis
answers.a4: Symptoms matter only at the first visit

midwifery-s3q1.question: A note says “left arm” but the handover says “right arm”. What needs clarification?

midwifery-s3q2.question: A measurement is written as “12” with no unit. What is missing?

answers.a3: The unit needed to interpret the value

midwifery-s3q3.question: Which record clearly separates a reported symptom from an observation?

answers.a2: “Nothing happened because the chart is blank”
answers.a4: “Definitely has a diagnosis I have not assessed”

midwifery-s3q4.question: Why include the time beside a new observation?

answers.a3: To place it in the sequence of events
answers.a4: To prove the cause by itself

midwifery-s3q5.question: A chart has no entry for a scheduled measurement. What can you conclude?

midwifery-s3q6.question: Which entry records what happened most clearly?

midwifery-s3q7.question: Why compare current observations with earlier ones?

answers.a1: To avoid looking at the person
answers.a3: To prove a diagnosis from any difference

midwifery-s4q3.question: Which stage of childbirth ends when the cervix is fully dilated?

midwifery-s4q4.question: Which stage runs from full cervical dilation to the baby’s birth?

midwifery-s4q5.question: The baby is born but the placenta has not yet been delivered. Which stage is this?

midwifery-s4q6.question: Which description is most useful when recording contractions?

midwifery-s4q7.question: Constant severe pain with faintness replaces previously comfortable pauses. What is safest?

answers.a1: Assume every later change must be expected
answers.a2: Seek urgent qualified assessment of the change
answers.a3: Wait for a planned routine check
answers.a4: Choose a diagnosis before reporting anything

midwifery-s5q1.question: What helps a stable newborn conserve warmth soon after birth?

answers.a3: Thorough drying and supported skin-to-skin care
answers.a4: Unnecessary exposure to a cool room

midwifery-s5q2.question: Why can leaving a newborn wet increase heat loss?

answers.a1: Evaporation removes heat from the skin
answers.a3: Water permanently blocks all heat loss

midwifery-s5q3.question: Which function needs assessment immediately after birth?

midwifery-s5q4.question: For a stable newborn having skin-to-skin care, what still matters?

answers.a1: Observation and keeping the airway clear

midwifery-s5q5.question: Which concern in a newborn calls for urgent qualified help?

answers.a1: A need for a clean blanket
answers.a2: A parent asking a routine question
answers.a3: A label needing a clearer font

midwifery-s5q6.question: What is the general aim of thermal care for a newborn?

answers.a4: Make the baby as hot as possible

midwifery-s5q7.question: A stable newborn has been dried, but the blanket is now wet. What supports warmth?

answers.a2: Use cold water to dry the skin
answers.a3: Expose the baby to a cold draft
answers.a4: Replace wet material with suitable dry covering

answers.a1: The early milk produced around the start of breastfeeding
answers.a2: A hormone made only by the placenta

midwifery-s6q2.question: Which behaviour can be an early feeding cue?

answers.a2: Turning toward touch near the mouth and seeking to suck

midwifery-s6q3.question: A newborn is feeding less and breathing noticeably faster. What is safest?

answers.a3: Assume the two changes cancel out
answers.a4: Wait until the next routine visit

midwifery-s6q4.question: A parent is struggling with feeding. What is the most helpful response?

answers.a1: Promise one method always works instantly
answers.a4: Listen and arrange appropriate feeding support

midwifery-s6q5.question: Which sleep position is recommended for most healthy babies?

answers.a4: Propped on their side with pillows

midwifery-s6q6.question: Which sleep space supports safer infant sleep?

answers.a2: A sofa cushion with loose blankets
answers.a4: A firm, flat sleep surface without loose soft items

midwifery-s6q7.question: A parent says their newborn is much less active than usual. What is appropriate?

answers.a1: Assume all reduced activity is normal sleep
answers.a2: Wait for every other symptom to appear
answers.a3: Ignore it if the baby was well yesterday
answers.a4: Take the change seriously and seek qualified assessment

midwifery-s7q1.question: Hands are visibly dirty. Which cleaning method is appropriate?

answers.a1: Put gloves on over the dirt

midwifery-s7q2.question: What should happen after protective gloves are removed?

answers.a1: Clean hands only if a glove tore
answers.a3: Keep the gloves for another person

midwifery-s7q3.question: Which container is designed for used needles and other sharps?

answers.a3: An open tray for later sorting

midwifery-s7q4.question: A task may splash body fluid toward the face. Which protection addresses that risk?

midwifery-s7q5.question: Shared observation equipment has been used. What should happen before reuse?

answers.a2: Clean it using the approved method
answers.a3: Use it unchanged if it looks shiny
answers.a4: Cover old marks with a label

midwifery-s7q6.question: A sterile package is torn before use. What is the safe conclusion?

answers.a1: The contents are sterile if they look clean
answers.a2: The printed date cancels the tear

midwifery-s7q7.question: Which statement about protective gloves is correct?

answers.a1: They stay clean regardless of what they touch
answers.a2: They do not replace hand hygiene
answers.a4: The same pair is suitable for every patient

midwifery-s8q1.question: A person says, “I’m worried about what happens next.” What is the best opening?

answers.a2: Acknowledge the worry and invite questions
answers.a3: Promise there is no possible risk

midwifery-s8q2.question: Someone wants to discuss a sensitive concern in a busy public area. What protects privacy?

answers.a3: Write the details on a public board

midwifery-s8q3.question: A person has not understood an explanation. What helps check understanding?

answers.a1: Treat a nod as proof of understanding
answers.a3: Ask another patient to answer for them
answers.a4: Explain plainly and ask them to describe it in their own words

midwifery-s8q4.question: Before a non-urgent examination, what should the person receive?

answers.a1: Only a form with no explanation
answers.a2: An assurance that questions are not allowed
answers.a3: A clear explanation and an opportunity to consent
answers.a4: A decision made by the nearest visitor

midwifery-s8q5.question: A person declines having students present. What is the respectful response?

answers.a2: Respect the choice and protect privacy
answers.a3: Assume silence later cancels the choice

midwifery-s8q6.question: A language barrier makes an important discussion difficult. What is the best support?

answers.a2: Asking a young child to interpret sensitive details

midwifery-s8q7.question: A person with hearing difficulty asks you to repeat yourself. What is helpful?

answers.a2: Face them and check their preferred way to communicate

midwifery-s9q1.question: A record shows 650 mL plus 250 mL. What is the total?

midwifery-s9q2.question: How many millilitres are in 1.5 L?

midwifery-s9q3.question: How much time passes from 09:20 to 10:05?

midwifery-s9q4.question: You count 9 breaths in 30 seconds. What is the equivalent rate per minute?

midwifery-s9q5.question: A recorded total rises from 600 mL to 900 mL. What is the percentage increase?

midwifery-s9q6.question: Divide 1.2 L equally across four recorded periods. How much belongs to each?

midwifery-s9q7.question: Three sealed boxes hold eight items each. How many items are there?

midwifery-s10q1.question: Which handover puts a new urgent concern first?

answers.a4: “New severe headache with visual changes; urgent review needed”

midwifery-s10q2.question: A person asks for time to consider a non-urgent care option. What respects their choice?

answers.a1: Ask a visitor to decide without permission
answers.a2: Explain the options and allow appropriate time for questions
answers.a4: Treat the request as automatic agreement

midwifery-s10q3.question: After birth, heavy bleeding occurs with faintness. What is the safest priority?

answers.a1: Assume bleeding cannot become serious after birth
answers.a3: Wait to see if the next day is better

midwifery-s10q4.question: A normal earlier record is followed by new breathing difficulty. Which information guides the response now?

answers.a2: The current change alongside the earlier record

midwifery-s10q5.question: A clean task follows handling contaminated equipment. What should happen before continuing?

answers.a1: Perform appropriate hand hygiene and change equipment or gloves as needed
answers.a2: Continue because both tasks are in the same room
answers.a4: Move contamination to a different tray

midwifery-s10q6.question: A concerned parent describes a change you did not witness. What is the useful response?

answers.a1: Dismiss it because you were not present
answers.a2: Ask them not to mention changes again
answers.a3: Listen, clarify the change and arrange assessment when needed
answers.a4: Record an unconfirmed diagnosis as fact

midwifery-s10q7.question: A fluid record shows 650 mL plus 450 mL. A separate pulse record rises from 74 to 82. Which summary is accurate?
